newsitem.title: USA: Tosco to meet with oil union.
newsitem.headline: Tosco to meet with oil union.

text.p: Tosco Corp has agreed to resume labour contract negotiations early on Monday with oil workers who are threatening to strike at four California refineries later in the day, a union official said.

"Tosco has called the (union) negotiating committee back to the table on Monday," said Howard Spencer, the president of the Rodeo, California, branch of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW).
The union represents 900 workers, roughly half the workforce, at four California refineries being bought by Tosco Corp from Unocal Corp at the end of the month.

Last week, the union negotiating team sent a letter to Unocal saying it might terminate its contract on March 24, giving its members the option to walk off the job. The union was protesting stalled severance talks.
Earlier in the week, the union also rejected a "final" contract offer from incoming owner Tosco, citing disagreements over a new contract and job cuts.
Spencer said Tosco contacted the union over the weekend and has agreed to meet with the its negotiating team around 10 a.m. (1800 GMT) on Monday in Los Angeles.
He said Tosco must be bringing something "worthwhile" to the table, otherwise the union would bar its negotiators from meeting with the company.
He also said the revived talks with Tosco could signal a revised offer from Unocal.
"We fully expect them to call us back to the table," he said.
